chapter.title: Scope
chapter.para: This specification defines a layered protocol stack that enables any ONVIF-compliant client to discover, configure, and consume data from any AI-enabled ONVIF-compliant device. The stack combines three open technologies:

listitem.para: ONVIF, for standardised device control;
MCP (Model Context Protocol), for standardised AI tool invocation and metadata streaming;
LinkML, for defining, validating, and sharing structured metadata schemas.

chapter.para: The document is divided into the following sections:
Scope: Defines the applicability and boundaries of this specification.
Building Blocks: Introduces the four constituent technologies — ONVIF, MCP, LinkML, and JSON-LD — and their individual roles in the stack.
Protocol Stack Architecture: Describes the overall layered architecture, the two planes, and the shared identity authority.
Service Discovery and Data Exchange: Defines the message sequences for connection establishment, schema retrieval, skill invocation, and metadata event delivery.
Authentication and Authorization: Specifies the JWT-based security model, ONVIF role mapping, and TLS requirements.

section.title: Background
section.para: Traditional physical-security systems are built around devices that expose predefined services, events, metadata, and configuration interfaces. ONVIF clients, including video management systems, use these interfaces to configure devices and ingest information into a site-centric operational view.

AI-enabled and agentic systems introduce additional consumers and interaction patterns. These systems need to discover available capabilities, retrieve contextual information, interpret semantically described data, and invoke permitted actions across devices, analytics services, and other site systems.

The ONVIF AI Service connects these environments. It complements existing ONVIF services by providing common information models and discovery mechanisms that can be used by both traditional clients and AI-native applications. Initial use cases include a VMS ingesting standardised site-centric metadata and an authorised AI application using MCP to discover and access device configuration capabilities.

section.title: Motivation
section.para: Without standardisation, AI integrations depend on vendor-specific data models, capability descriptions, and agent tools. This increases integration cost and limits portability across manufacturers and system components.

This specification defines the interoperable boundary between information producers and consumers. It enables consistent exchange of semantic metadata, provenance, confidence, spatial and temporal context, and capability descriptions, while reusing existing ONVIF services and security mechanisms where applicable.

The objective is not to prescribe a complete AI architecture or replace established VMS workflows. The objective is to allow traditional physical-security systems and AI-native systems to share trusted information and expose controlled functionality through standardised contracts.

chapter.title: Overview
chapter.para: AI configurations are handled through the ai service. AI configurations are used to configure and control the intelligent functions as defined in this specification. The device provides AI configuration through the AI service. WSDL for this service is specified in http://www.onvif.org/ver20/media/wsdl/media.wsdll.

section.title: MCP — The AI Tool Interface
section.para: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open, JSON-RPC 2.0 based protocol designed to connect AI language models and agents to external tools and data sources. In the ONVIF AI stack, MCP serves as the standardised interface layer between the ONVIF Client (acting as an MCP Host) and each ONVIF Device (acting as an MCP Server). Adopting MCP means that any ONVIF Client can invoke any compliant ONVIF Device without requiring a vendor-specific driver.

section.title: Protocol Primitives
section.para: MCP defines three categories of server-side object that a host may discover and use:

listitem.para: Tools are callable operations with a named identifier, a human-readable description, and an inputSchema (JSON Schema) that fully describes the expected arguments. In the ONVIF AI stack, Tools are called Skills and represent ONVIF Device capabilities such as configuring a detection region or querying service status. The ONVIF Client invokes a Skill by sending a tools/call JSON-RPC request over the Control Plane.

Resources are read-only data objects accessible via resources/list and resources/read requests. In this specification, Resources carry the LinkML schema bundles that describe the event payloads and skill input parameters of the ONVIF Device. Each schema resource carries the MIME type application/linkml+yaml.
Prompts are optional server-defined interaction templates. This specification does not mandate Prompt support; ONVIF Devices MAY expose Prompts for human-in-the-loop workflows.

section.title: Transport Modes
section.para: This specification normatively uses the Streamable HTTP transport. The ONVIF Client sends JSON-RPC requests as HTTP POST to the ONVIF Device's /mcp endpoint. For server-initiated messages (schema update notifications, metadata events) the ONVIF Client also opens a Streamable HTTP channel on /mcp; the ONVIF Device sends server-initiated messages over that channel as defined by the Streamable HTTP transport in MCP 2026-07-28. An ONVIF Device conforming to this specification shall support the Streamable HTTP transport.

section.title: Protocol Version
section.para: This specification normatively requires MCP 2026-07-28. Implementations conforming to this specification shall not use the session-era MCP 2025-11-25 protocol.

MCP 2026-07-28 is a fully stateless protocol. There is no session establishment handshake and no Mcp-Session-Id header. Every HTTP request is self-contained: the ONVIF Client includes the MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28 request header on each call, together with the Authorization: Bearer JWT header. The ONVIF Device shall reject requests that carry a protocol version other than 2026-07-28 with HTTP 400.

Service discovery uses the server/discover JSON-RPC method, which replaces the initialize / initialized handshake of earlier versions. The response carries the server's capability flags (tools, resources, prompts) and its human-readable identity. As required by MCP 2026-07-28, the ONVIF Device shall implement server/discover. The ONVIF Client may call server/discover before issuing other requests to learn supported versions and capabilities, but it is not required to call it first and may invoke any operation directly and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.

The stateless model is the correct choice for the ONVIF AI use case: ONVIF Devices are deployed as horizontally-scalable endpoints behind load balancers, and pinning a ONVIF Client to a specific server instance via a session identifier would prevent transparent failover and scaling. With MCP 2026-07-28, every request can be routed to any instance of the ONVIF Device without loss of state.

section.title: LinkML — Schema Definition Language
section.para: LinkML (Linked data Modeling Language) is an open schema definition language that describes data structures in YAML. In the ONVIF AI stack, LinkML is the normative language for defining both the structure of metadata events (Event Plane payloads) and the argument shapes of Skills (Control Plane inputs). LinkML defines the schema; JSON-LD (see ) is the runtime wire format that carries instances of that schema.

section.title: Schema Structure
section.para: A LinkML schema document is a YAML file with the following top-level keys:

listitem.para: id: a globally unique URI that serves as the schema identifier. This URI is reused as the JSON-LD @context value in every event payload emitted by the ONVIF Device, making the schema self-locating.

imports: a list of schema URIs from which common types are inherited. ONVIF maintains a shared type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines reusable structures such as bounding boxes, polygon regions, timestamps, and confidence scores. ONVIF Devices SHOULD import this library rather than redefining common types.

classes: named data structures with typed attributes, optional range constraints (minimum_value, maximum_value), and documentation strings. The root event class shall extend BaseAnalyticsEvent from the ONVIF common type library.
enums: closed value sets used for categorical fields such as SeverityLevel (low, medium, high, critical) and event type discriminators.

section.title: Dual Role: Event Schema and Skill Input Schema
section.para: The same LinkML model serves two distinct purposes within the stack:

listitem.para: On the Event Plane, the compiled JSON Schema derived from the LinkML model is used by the ONVIF Client LinkML Validator to check every incoming metadata event for structural correctness — required fields, numeric ranges, and valid enum values.

On the Control Plane, the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool (Skill) definition is also derived from the same LinkML model. This guarantees that the coordinate spaces, unit definitions, and vocabulary used to configure the ONVIF Device (e.g., a detection region polygon) are identical to those used to report events, eliminating a class of integration errors that arise when configuration and reporting use incompatible data models.

section.title: Compilation to JSON Schema
section.para: The LinkML toolchain provides a generator that produces a JSON Schema document from a LinkML YAML source. This compiled JSON Schema is used in two places:

listitem.para: First, it is embedded in the inputSchema field of each MCP Tool definition returned by tools/list. The ONVIF Client can validate skill arguments against this schema before sending a tools/call request, providing early client-side error detection.

Second, a copy of the compiled schema is stored in the ONVIF Client Schema Registry after schema discovery. The registry uses the compiled schema to validate every incoming metadata event on the Event Plane before the ONVIF Client processes it.

section.para: ONVIF Devices shall pre-compile their LinkML schemas at build time and include the compiled JSON Schema in Tool definitions. The source YAML shall also be exposed as a schema Resource so that the ONVIF Client can re-compile or audit the schema independently.

section.title: ONVIF Common Type Library
section.para: The ONVIF AI Working Group maintains a shared LinkML type library (ver10_schema_common_linkml) that defines base classes and enumerations used across all ONVIF Devices. Key types include:

BaseAnalyticsEvent: the mandatory root class for all metadata events, defining the required fields event_id (UUID), timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), source_uri, confidence (float, 0.0–1.0), and severity (SeverityLevel enum).
BoundingBox and PolygonRegion: normalised coordinate structures shared between event payloads and skill input schemas to ensure consistent spatial referencing.

ONVIF shall not redefine any type declared in the common type library. This ensures that an ONVIF Client that has already loaded the common library does not need to re-fetch it for each new ONVIF Device it connects to.

section.title: JSON-LD — Wire Format for Metadata Events
section.para: JSON-LD (JSON-based Linked Data) is the serialisation format used for all metadata events transmitted on the Event Plane. Where LinkML defines the schema at design time, JSON-LD carries instances of that schema at runtime. The two technologies are complementary: LinkML declares what data looks like; JSON-LD is the payload that conforms to that declaration.

section.title: Context and Type Annotations
section.para: Every metadata event emitted by an ONVIF Device shall include two mandatory JSON-LD keywords:

@context: a URI that points to the canonical LinkML schema for this event type. The value shall equal the id field of the LinkML schema from which the event class is derived. This URI is the primary key used by the ONVIF Client Schema Registry to look up the compiled JSON Schema for validation.

@type: the class name of the event as declared in the LinkML schema (e.g., FireDetectionEvent, PersonCrossingEvent). This field allows the ONVIF Client to route the event to the appropriate handler without inspecting the full payload.

Together, @context and @type make each event self-describing: an ONVIF Client that receives an event with an unfamiliar @context URI knows exactly where to fetch the schema needed to understand and validate the event.

section.title: Self-Describing Events and Dynamic Schema Registration
section.para: The self-describing nature of JSON-LD enables a dynamic schema registration workflow. When the ONVIF Client Schema Registry (Layer 2) receives a metadata event whose @context URI does not match any registered schema, it SHOULD:
1. Suspend validation of the triggering event.
2. Fetch the LinkML schema YAML from the URI identified by @context, or issue an MCP resources/read request to the originating ONVIF Device to retrieve the latest schema bundle.
3. Register the schema bundle in the local registry.
4. Re-validate and process the suspended event against the newly registered schema.

This mechanism allows an ONVIF Device to introduce a new event type (e.g., a firmware update that adds a VehicleTypeDetectionEvent) without requiring a pre-coordinated ONVIF Client update. The ONVIF Client self-heals its schema knowledge at runtime.

section.title: Relationship to Linked Data
section.para: Although full JSON-LD processing (graph expansion, context dereferencing, SPARQL querying) is not required by this specification, the use of JSON-LD framing ensures forward compatibility with semantic web tooling. A conformant ONVIF Client shall treat @context and @type as opaque identifiers for schema lookup and event routing. An ONVIF Client MAY additionally perform full JSON-LD processing for downstream applications such as knowledge graph ingestion or cross-vendor event correlation.

section.title: Architecture Overview
section.para: The ONVIF AI Protocol Stack is structured around the standard ONVIF roles of an ONVIF Client and an ONVIF Device, with an OIDC Authorization Server acting as the shared trust anchor that issues the tokens consumed by both. The figure below shows the top-level relationships between these three components and the two communication planes.

figure.title: ONVIF AI Protocol Stack — Top-Level Architecture

section.para: The OIDC Authorization Server is the trust anchor for the entire stack. It issues signed ES256 JWTs to the ONVIF Client via the OAuth2 Client Credentials grant, and exposes a JWKS endpoint that the ONVIF Device uses to validate every token it receives.

The ONVIF Client combines the ONVIF Client role with the MCP Host role. It manages connections to ONVIF Devices, invokes skills, and subscribes to metadata events. It also maintains the LinkML Schema Registry and validates every incoming event before it is passed to business logic.

The ONVIF Device provides an MCP Server endpoint. Through this endpoint, it exposes skills in the form of MCP Tools and publishes JSON-LD metadata events. Moreover, it announces the LinkML schema via MCP Resources.

All communication between the ONVIF Client and the ONVIF Device is bearer-token authenticated. The Control Plane (A) carries MCP tools/call requests from the ONVIF Client to the ONVIF Device. The Event Plane (B) carries JSON-LD metadata events from the ONVIF Device to the ONVIF Client, delivered as MCP notifications/message frames.

section.title: Protocol Stack
section.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack uses two independent communication planes, both protected by TLS and bearer tokens issued by the OIDC Authorization Server. The Control Plane carries client-initiated MCP requests, while the Event Plane carries server-pushed metadata events. The detailed behavior of each plane is defined in the following sections.

section.title: Control Plane
section.para: The Control Plane is the command path used by the ONVIF Client to discover and invoke Skills exposed by an ONVIF Device. It is request/response oriented and carries only client-initiated MCP operations.

entry.para: Discover capabilities, list skills, and invoke device actions.
HTTP POST to /mcp over HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2.
server/discover, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, and resources/read.
TLS 1.3 with an Authorization: Bearer ES256 JWT on every request.

section.para: Each request is self-contained and shall be validated independently by the ONVIF Device before execution. A Control Plane response shall report either the requested result or an MCP error indicating why the operation could not be completed.

section.title: Metadata Event Plane
section.para: The Metadata Event Plane is the event path used by the ONVIF Device to publish AI analytics results to the ONVIF Client. It is server-initiated, asynchronous, and optimized for continuous delivery of structured metadata events.

entry.para: Deliver detection and analytics events as they occur.
Streamable HTTP to /mcp endpoint, as defined by MCP 2026-07-28.
JSON-LD events conforming to the registered LinkML schema.
TLS 1.3 with an Authorization: Bearer ES256 JWT on every request.

section.para: The Event Plane shall preserve event ordering per stream, and each event shall remain self-describing through its JSON-LD @context and @type annotations.

section.title: Identity and Authorization Server
section.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack requires an OAuth 2.1 Authorization Server, as specified in the ONVIF Security Service Specification.

This server acts as the trust anchor for the complete stack: it authenticates clients, issues bearer access tokens, and exposes the metadata and key material needed by ONVIF Devices to validate tokens before processing MCP requests.

In practice, the Authorization Server provides centralized identity and access control for both planes. It ensures that only authorized ONVIF Clients can invoke Skills on the Control Plane and receive protected metadata on the Event Plane, according to the roles and claims contained in the issued token.

section.title: Network Discovery
section.para: MCP 2026-07-28 does not define network-level device discovery. Therefore, ONVIF Device discovery remains dependent on the mechanisms specified by [ONVIF Core]. An ONVIF Client shall discover ONVIF Devices and obtain their service endpoint using the ONVIF Core discovery procedures before initiating MCP requests.

section.title: Service Discovery
section.para: An ONVIF Device that supports the AI Service shall advertise the MCP service endpoint URL through the ONVIF Core service discovery mechanism. In the ONVIF Core GetServices response, the corresponding AI Service entry (tds:GetServiceResponse) shall contain the service address used by the ONVIF Client for MCP requests.

section.title: Session Initialization
section.para: An ONVIF Device implementing the AI Service shall implement the server/discover JSON-RPC method as required by MCP 2026-07-28. The ONVIF Client MAY call server/discover as its first request on a new connection to obtain the device's protocol version, server identity, and capability flags. Alternatively, the ONVIF Client MAY call any other operation directly and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (JSON-RPC error code -32022) if the protocol version is not supported. In that case the ONVIF Device shall include a supported list in the error response and the ONVIF Client shall retry using one of the listed versions.

The server/discover response shall contain: protocolVersions — the list of MCP protocol versions supported by the device; identity — the server name and version; capabilities — the declared capability flags (tools, resources, prompts). The ONVIF Client shall use the returned capabilities flags to determine which subsequent operations are available before invoking them.

The ONVIF Client shall open the Streamable HTTP channel as defined by MCP 2026-07-28 before it expects to receive notifications/message frames from the ONVIF Device. This channel shall remain open for the duration of the session. See for wire format examples.

section.title: Schema Retrieval
section.para: The ONVIF AI Service exposes its LinkML metadata schema as one or more MCP Resources. An ONVIF Client shall retrieve the schema bundle before processing any notifications/message frame that carries metadata events.

The schema retrieval procedure is:
The ONVIF Client calls resources/list. The response includes one or more resources with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml identifying the schema files.
The ONVIF Client calls resources/read for each schema resource URI returned in step 1, in the order listed. A schema bundle may span multiple resources when imported type definitions are split across files.
The ONVIF Client registers the complete schema bundle in its validator.

An ONVIF Device shall advertise at least one resource with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml describing the structure of every event type it emits. The schema shall be self-contained — it shall not require the ONVIF Client to resolve external URIs to validate event payloads.
See and for wire format examples.

section.title: Capability Discovery
section.para: Capability discovery shall be performed through the MCP resources/read operation using the reserved URI capabilities://onvif/ai.

An ONVIF Device implementing the AI Service shall expose capabilities://onvif/ai and shall return the AI Service capabilities document when that URI is requested via resources/read. The capabilities document describes the features supported by the device, such as supported analytics types, event classes, and optional extensions.
Exposing capabilities for other ONVIF services is optional. When provided, the same URI pattern shall be used, replacing ai with the service name: capabilities://onvif/<service-name>.
See and for wire format examples.

section.title: Tool Discovery
section.para: The ONVIF Device exposes its Skills — callable operations — as MCP Tools. The ONVIF Client discovers the available Skills by calling tools/list.

Each Tool entry in the tools/list response shall contain:
name — the Skill identifier used in subsequent tools/call requests.
description — a human-readable description of the Skill's function.
inputSchema — a JSON Schema object that fully describes the expected arguments. This JSON Schema is compiled from the LinkML model retrieved in and shall use the same coordinate spaces, unit definitions, and vocabulary as the event payloads delivered over the Event Plane.

The ONVIF Client shall validate Skill arguments against the inputSchema before sending a tools/call request. After completing tool discovery the ONVIF Client has obtained, without any out-of-band documentation: the complete catalogue of Skills supported by this device instance; the argument types, valid ranges, and required/optional fields for each Skill; and human-readable descriptions suitable for display or automated orchestration.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: Skill Invocation
section.para: ONVIF AI Skills are invoked via the MCP tools/call JSON-RPC method over the Control Plane. The ONVIF Device shall validate the arguments object against the inputSchema of the named Skill before executing it. If validation fails, the ONVIF Device shall return a structured error response without executing the Skill.

This specification defines three mandatory Skills that every ONVIF AI Device shall implement regardless of device type (camera, NVR, access control, or other). Additional device-type-specific Skills may be defined in ONVIF profiles or vendor extensions.

section.title: get_status
section.para: The get_status Skill returns the current operational status of the AI analytics engine. It takes no arguments. The ONVIF Device shall always respond successfully to this Skill unless the device is unreachable.

The response structuredContent shall include:
state — one of running, stopped, degraded, or error.
activeAnalytics — list of analytics type identifiers currently active on the device.
engineVersion — version string of the AI engine firmware.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: list_analytics
section.para: The list_analytics Skill returns the set of analytics types supported by this device instance, together with their current enabled/disabled state. It takes no arguments. This is the authoritative machine-readable catalogue of what this device can do; the ONVIF Client shall call list_analytics before calling configure_analytics.

Each entry in the response structuredContent.analytics array shall include:
type — analytics type identifier drawn from the ONVIF AI analytics type vocabulary (for example fire_detection, face_recognition, license_plate_recognition, tailgating_detection).
enabled — boolean indicating whether this analytics type is currently active.
configSchema — URI of the LinkML class in the schema bundle (retrieved in ) that defines the structure of the config argument accepted by configure_analytics for this type.
An ONVIF Device that executes no analytics locally (for example a pure RFID access control reader) shall return an empty analytics array.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: configure_analytics
section.para: The configure_analytics Skill applies a configuration to a named analytics type. It is a generic wrapper: the structure of the config argument is defined by the LinkML schema class identified by the configSchema URI returned by list_analytics for that type. The ONVIF Client shall validate config against the compiled JSON Schema (the inputSchema of the Skill) before sending the request.

The configure_analytics Skill arguments are:
analytics_type (string, required) — the analytics type identifier, as returned by list_analytics.
config (object, required) — the configuration object whose structure is specific to analytics_type and defined by the corresponding LinkML schema class.
On success the ONVIF Device shall confirm the applied configuration. On failure it shall return a structured error identifying the failing field and the violated constraint.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: Streamable HTTP Delivery Mode
section.para: The ONVIF Device delivers metadata events as MCP notifications/message frames over the Streamable HTTP channel established during session initialization (). Event delivery is push-only: the ONVIF Device sends frames autonomously as observations are produced; the ONVIF Client does not poll.

The ONVIF Client shall open the Streamable HTTP channel before invoking configure_analytics to enable an analytics type. Each notifications/message frame shall carry exactly one metadata event. Batch delivery of multiple events in a single frame is not permitted.

When the Streamable HTTP channel is closed, the ONVIF Device shall retain pending metadata events in a FIFO buffer until the buffer capacity is exhausted. When the buffer is full, the oldest event shall be discarded to make room for the newest. If the ONVIF Client reopens the Streamable HTTP channel before the buffer is exhausted, the ONVIF Device shall deliver all buffered events in FIFO order before resuming live delivery. If the buffer is exhausted before the client reconnects, delivery continuity is lost and the ONVIF Client shall treat the gap as a potential loss of events.

The buffer capacity of the device is advertised in the capabilities://onvif/ai document via the eventBufferCapacity field (integer, number of events). A value of 0 indicates that the device does not support buffering; events produced while the channel is closed are discarded immediately.

section.title: Dynamic Schema Re-registration
section.para:
The @context URI in each event is a live pointer to the schema that defines it. If the ONVIF Client receives a notifications/message frame whose @context URI is not already registered in its schema bundle, it shall:
Suspend validation of that event without discarding it.
Call resources/read with the @context URI to fetch the LinkML schema YAML from the ONVIF Device.
Register the retrieved schema in its validator.
Resume validation of the suspended event and all subsequent events of that type.

This mechanism allows the ONVIF Device to introduce new event types — for example after a firmware update — without requiring the ONVIF Client to have prior knowledge of the new schema. The ONVIF Device shall ensure that the @context URI is always resolvable via resources/read for as long as the device emits events of that type.
See for a wire format example.

section.title: Post-Handshake ONVIF Client Knowledge
section.para: An ONVIF AI Service is self-describing: an ONVIF Client that has completed the sequence defined in Sections 7.3 through 7.5 is fully operational without any out-of-band documentation, SDK, or static configuration. The table below summarises the knowledge accumulated at each step.

entry.para: Device identity, supported protocol versions, declared capability flags (resources, tools).
Complete LinkML schema bundle; JSON Schema for event validation and skill argument validation.
Device feature set, supported analytics types, eventBufferCapacity.
Skill catalogue: name, human-readable description, and inputSchema for each skill.
Which analytics types are currently enabled; configSchema URI per analytics type.
Live metadata events; @type for routing; @context for dynamic schema re-registration.

section.para: An ONVIF Device implementing this specification shall ensure that an ONVIF Client completing the above sequence is able to: validate all incoming event payloads against the registered schema; invoke any available Skill with correctly structured arguments; and interpret the full feature set of the device — all without consulting any resource external to the ONVIF Device.

chapter.title: Authentication and Authorization
chapter.para: The ONVIF AI protocol stack delegates all authentication and token management to the mechanisms defined in the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. Those documents govern JWT token format and required claims (iss, aud, exp, nbf, roles), the mandatory ES256 signing algorithm, token validation rules, the OAuth2 Client Credentials flow, authorization server configuration, and TLS transport requirements. Implementations not comply with the ONVIF Core Specification and the ONVIF Security Service Specification. This chapter defines only the ONVIF AI-specific normative mapping of MCP operations to ONVIF access classes.

section.title: Role-to-MCP Operation Mapping
section.para: The ONVIF Security Service Specification defines three predefined JWT role values carried in the roles claim of every access token: onvif:User, onvif:Operator, and onvif:Administrator. These correspond to the ONVIF user levels and cover the majority of deployments. For environments that require finer-grained access control, the Security Service Specification defines a full user role management model that allows custom roles to be assigned to individual users; refer to the ONVIF Security Service Specification for details. The onvif: namespace prefix is reserved; custom roles shall not use it.

Anonymous access to any MCP endpoint is not permitted. Every request to the ONVIF Device shall carry a valid Authorization: Bearer JWT. The ONVIF Device maps the access class required by each MCP operation against the roles claim in the presented token and rejects requests that do not satisfy the minimum role requirement with HTTP 403. A token carrying onvif:Administrator satisfies all lower access class requirements; a token carrying onvif:Operator satisfies READ_SYSTEM in addition to ACTUATE.
The table below is normative. Each Skill exposed via tools/list shall include an annotation declaring its access class. The ONVIF Device shall enforce this mapping at runtime.

table.title: MCP Operation Access Class and Minimum Role Requirements

entry.para: tools/call — administrative Skills (e.g. model management, device configuration)

chapter.title: Metadata
chapter.para: This chapter defines the data model for structured metadata produced and consumed by ONVIF AI-enabled devices. All metadata payloads are instances of, or derived from, the abstract classes defined here. The normative schema is expressed in LinkML; JSON-LD is the wire format (see ).

section.title: Observation
section.para: Observation is the top-level abstract container for every piece of information emitted by an ONVIF AI Device. Because AI services produce heterogeneous outputs — object detection results, fire alerts, people counts, anomaly reports — the class is intentionally abstract: domain-specific event classes derive from it and add their own semantic fields. An ONVIF Device shall serialise every AI metadata payload as an instance of a class that directly or transitively extends Observation.

Every Observation instance carries a mandatory unique identifier and a creation timestamp. Three optional nested objects — Provenance, Location, and Timing — provide contextual metadata about authenticity, spatial origin, and temporal reference respectively. Each is defined by an abstract class; concrete implementations are described in the following sections.

section.title: SOSAObservation
section.para: SOSAObservation is the first concrete subclass of Observation defined by this specification. It aligns the ONVIF AI metadata model with the W3C Semantic Sensor Network (SSN) / SOSA ontology (https://www.w3.org/TR/vocab-ssn/), enabling interoperability with the broader Linked Data and IoT ecosystem.

SOSA defines an Observation as an act carried out by a Sensor that produces a Result whose value estimates or calculates a value of an ObservableProperty of a FeatureOfInterest. The SOSAObservation class maps these four SOSA roles directly to ONVIF AI Device semantics:

listitem.para: madeBySensor — the ONVIF AI component (camera, analytics module, or AI inference engine) that produced the observation. Corresponds to sosa:madeBySensor.
observedProperty — the physical or logical property being measured or inferred (for example onvif:PersonCount, onvif:FlamePresence). Corresponds to sosa:observedProperty.
hasFeatureOfInterest — the real-world entity about which the observation is made (for example a scene, a zone, or a specific object). Corresponds to sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest.
hasResult — the structured result object that is the outcome of the observation. Shall be an instance of a concrete subclass of ObservationResult. Corresponds to sosa:hasResult.

phenomenonTime — the time interval or instant during which the observed property held the reported value. Distinct from the observation creation timestamp inherited from Observation. Corresponds to sosa:phenomenonTime.
resultTime — the instant at which the result became available (the observation was completed). Corresponds to sosa:resultTime.
usedProcedure — the AI algorithm or procedure applied by the sensor to produce the result (optional). Corresponds to sosa:usedProcedure.

section.para: All four mandatory fields (madeBySensor, observedProperty, hasFeatureOfInterest, and hasResult) shall be present in every serialised SOSAObservation instance. The ONVIF AI Device shall use sosa: URIs as JSON-LD property keys to ensure full alignment with the SOSA ontology.

sosa:hasResult shall be an instance of a concrete subclass of ObservationResult appropriate for the event type. The provenance field is optional. When present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass of Provenance (). For deployments requiring integrity protection, JLDSProvenance () shall be used.

section.title: Provenance
section.para: Provenance is an abstract class nested within Observation that describes the authenticity and chain-of-custody of the observation. Because different deployment environments require different attestation mechanisms — cryptographic signatures, hash-of-source-frame, hardware attestation tokens, or simple device identity — the class is abstract and shall be specialised for each mechanism. Concrete subclasses add the fields specific to their attestation method.
The presence of a Provenance object is optional. When omitted, no authenticity claim is made for the observation.

section.title: JLDSProvenance
section.para: JLDSProvenance is the first concrete subclass of Provenance. It attests the integrity of an Observation by means of a JSON-LD Data Integrity proof [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. The ECC signature algorithm and key parameters shall conform to the ONVIF Security Baseline [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].

section.title: Signing procedure
section.para: The ONVIF Device shall compute the proof using the Add Proof algorithm defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY] with RDFC-1.0 [RDFC-1.0] as the canonicalization algorithm. The digest and signing algorithms shall be those mandated by the current version of [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].

section.title: Proof fields
section.para: JLDSProvenance carries the following fields, aligned with the DataIntegrityProof structure defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]:

listitem.para: type (mandatory) — fixed string "DataIntegrityProof".

cryptosuite (mandatory) — identifies the cryptosuite used. The value shall correspond to the algorithm profile mandated by the current version of [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. It is included in the proof configuration and therefore covered by the signature.
created (mandatory) — ISO 8601 UTC datetime at which the proof was created.
verificationMethod (mandatory) — URI of the public key or verification method that can be used to verify the proof.
proofPurpose (mandatory) — fixed string "assertionMethod".
proofValue (mandatory) — the encoded digital signature over hashData as defined in the signing procedure above.

section.title: Location
section.para: Location is an abstract class nested within Observation that represents the spatial origin of the observation. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: GeoLocation
section.para: GeoLocation is the first concrete subclass of Location. It expresses geographic position using WGS 84 coordinates obtained from a GPS receiver integrated in, or connected to, the ONVIF Device. It carries latitude and longitude as mandatory fields and an optional altitude above mean sea level.

section.title: Timing
section.para: Timing is an abstract class nested within Observation that provides an authoritative time reference for the observation, independent of the device system clock. It is optional; when present it shall be an instance of a concrete subclass.

section.title: GPSTiming
section.para: GPSTiming is the first concrete subclass of Timing. It carries the UTC timestamp extracted directly from the GPS signal, giving a traceable, drift-free time reference. An optional UTC offset field allows representation of local time where required.

section.title: Observation Result
section.para: ObservationResult is an abstract class that represents the outcome produced by an Observation. It corresponds to sosa:Result in the SOSA ontology and serves as the mandatory base type for the hasResult slot of SOSAObservation.

SOSA deliberately leaves the internal structure of a Result undefined, delegating its specification to the domain of application. In this specification ObservationResult plays that role: it is abstract and carries no fields of its own. All concrete AI result payloads shall be instances of a class that directly or transitively extends ObservationResult.

Concrete subclasses shall set the JSON-LD @type field to an unambiguous URI so that receivers can determine the result type without out-of-band knowledge. Future revisions of this specification, or vendor-specific extensions via the Extensible mixin, shall introduce concrete subclasses for specific AI output types (for example object detection bounding boxes, classification scores, or people counts).

section.title: Vendor Extensions
section.para: ONVIF follows the convention, established in its WSDL-based specifications, of providing a generic extension point in every data structure to allow implementers to carry vendor-specific information without breaking interoperability. This specification carries that convention into the LinkML metadata model through the Extensible mixin.

The Extensible mixin adds a single optional, repeatable slot named extension to any class that includes it. Each entry in the slot is an instance of VendorExtension, which pairs a mandatory vendor namespace URI with a locally named, arbitrarily typed value. The namespace URI uniquely identifies the vendor and prevents naming collisions between different implementers.

An ONVIF Client that encounters an extension entry whose vendor_namespace it does not recognise shall ignore that entry and shall not treat its presence as an error. An ONVIF Device shall not use the extension slot to carry information that is required for correct interpretation of the normative fields of the enclosing class.

The Extensible mixin is applied to Observation, making the extension point available on every concrete observation class derived from it. Other abstract classes in this chapter (Provenance, Location, Timing) may also include the mixin in future revisions as needed.

section.title: Normative LinkML Schema
section.para: This section is here just because it is handy now, it will be removed before releasing the specs.

The following LinkML YAML fragment is normative. All abstract classes are marked abstract: true; concrete subclasses set is_a to their parent. Fields marked required: true shall be present in every serialised instance; all other fields are optional.
section.programlisting:
id: https://www.onvif.org/ver10/ai/linkml/metadata name: onvif-ai-metadata description: ONVIF AI Metadata base schema prefixes: linkml: https://w3id.org/linkml/ sosa: http://www.w3.org/ns/sosa/ ssn: http://www.w3.org/ns/ssn/ onvif: https://www.onvif.org/ver10/ai/linkml/metadata/ imports: - linkml:types
classes:
VendorExtension: description: >- Container for a single vendor-specific extension entry. Analogous to xs:any in ONVIF WSDL extension elements. The vendor_namespace URI uniquely identifies the vendor and prevents naming collisions. attributes: vendor_namespace: range: uri required: true description: >- URI namespace that uniquely identifies the vendor (e.g. "https://acme.com/onvif/ext/v1"). name: range: string required: true description: >- Local name of the extension element within the vendor namespace. value: range: Any required: false description: >- Vendor-specific payload. May be a JSON object, string, or numeric value. ONVIF Clients shall ignore entries with unknown namespaces.
Extensible: mixin: true description: >- Mixin that adds a standard vendor extension point to any ONVIF class, following the xs:any convention of ONVIF WSDL specifications. attributes: extension: range: VendorExtension multivalued: true inlined_as_list: true required: false description: >- Zero or more vendor-specific extension entries. Clients shall ignore entries with unrecognised vendor_namespace values.
Observation: abstract: true mixins: - Extensible description: >- Top-level abstract container for every AI metadata payload emitted by an ONVIF Device. Domain-specific event classes shall extend this class. attributes: id: range: uriorcurie required: true description: Globally unique identifier for this observation instance. timestamp: range: datetime required: true description: >- Creation time of the observation, expressed as an ISO 8601 datetime in UTC. provenance: range: Provenance required: false description: >- Authenticity and chain-of-custody descriptor. Omitted when no attestation claim is made. location: range: Location required: false description: Spatial origin of the observation. timing: range: Timing required: false description: Authoritative time reference for the observation.
Provenance: abstract: true description: >- Abstract descriptor for the authenticity and chain-of-custody of an Observation. Concrete subclasses add attestation-method-specific fields.
Location: abstract: true description: >- Abstract spatial descriptor for an Observation. Concrete subclasses supply the coordinate system and position fields.
GeoLocation: is_a: Location description: >- WGS 84 geographic position obtained from a GPS receiver attached to or integrated in the ONVIF Device. attributes: latitude: range: double required: true minimum_value: -90.0 maximum_value: 90.0 description: Geodetic latitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). longitude: range: double required: true minimum_value: -180.0 maximum_value: 180.0 description: Geodetic longitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). altitude: range: double required: false description: Altitude above mean sea level in metres (WGS 84).
Timing: abstract: true description: >- Abstract authoritative time reference for an Observation, independent of the device system clock. Concrete subclasses specify the time source.
GPSTiming: is_a: Timing description: >- UTC timestamp extracted directly from the GPS signal, providing a traceable, drift-free time reference. attributes: gps_timestamp: range: datetime required: true description: UTC time extracted from the GPS signal (ISO 8601). utc_offset: range: string required: false description: >- UTC offset of the local time zone at the observation site, expressed as ±HH:MM (e.g. "+02:00"). Informative only.
JLDSProvenance: is_a: Provenance description: >- Concrete Provenance subclass that attests Observation integrity using a JSON-LD Data Integrity proof [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. The ECC signature algorithm and key parameters shall conform to [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. The proof is computed over the RDFC-1.0 canonical form of the Observation with the provenance field excluded. attributes: type: range: string required: true equals_string: "DataIntegrityProof" description: >- Fixed value "DataIntegrityProof" as defined in [VC-DATA-INTEGRITY]. cryptosuite: range: string required: true description: >- Identifies the cryptosuite used. The value shall be consistent with the ECC algorithm mandated by [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline]. created: range: datetime required: true description: ISO 8601 UTC datetime at which the proof was created. verificationMethod: range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI of the public key or verification method used to verify the proof. proofPurpose: range: string required: true equals_string: "assertionMethod" description: >- Fixed value "assertionMethod", indicating the proof asserts the content of the observation. proofValue: range: string required: true description: >- Encoded digital signature over hashData = H(canonical(unsecuredDocument)) || H(canonical(proofConfig)), where unsecuredDocument is the Observation with provenance removed, proofConfig is the proof object without proofValue, and H and the signing algorithm are mandated by [ONVIF-SecurityBaseline].
ObservationResult: abstract: true class_uri: sosa:Result description: >- Abstract base class for all AI observation result payloads. Corresponds to sosa:Result in the SOSA ontology. Concrete subclasses shall define the domain-specific fields (e.g. bounding boxes, classification scores, counts) and shall set @type to an unambiguous URI so that receivers can determine the result type without out-of-band knowledge.

Instances shall be serialised using sosa: property URIs as JSON-LD keys. class_uri: sosa:Observation attributes: madeBySensor: slot_uri: sosa:madeBySensor range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the ONVIF AI component (camera, analytics module, or inference engine) that produced this observation. observedProperty: slot_uri: sosa:observedProperty range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the physical or logical property being measured or inferred (e.g. onvif:PersonCount, onvif:FlamePresence). hasFeatureOfInterest: slot_uri: sosa:hasFeatureOfInterest range: uriorcurie required: true description: >- URI identifying the real-world entity about which the observation is made (e.g. a scene, a detection zone, or a specific object). hasResult: slot_uri: sosa:hasResult range: ObservationResult required: true description: >- The structured result object produced by the observation. Shall be an instance of a concrete subclass of ObservationResult. phenomenonTime: slot_uri: sosa:phenomenonTime range: datetime required: false description: >- The time instant or interval during which the observed property held the reported value. May differ from the Observation timestamp. resultTime: slot_uri: sosa:resultTime range: datetime required: false description: >- The instant at which the result became available (observation completed). Corresponds to sosa:resultTime. usedProcedure: slot_uri: sosa:usedProcedure range: uriorcurie required: false description: >- URI identifying the AI algorithm or procedure applied by the sensor to produce the result.

appendix.title: Example Call Sequence (informative)
appendix.para: This annex is informative and provides an example end-to-end sequence with sample values.

section.title: Network discovery (ONVIF Core)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends ONVIF Core discovery requests (for example WS-Discovery Probe) to locate devices on the network.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns discovery responses (for example ProbeMatches) with the Device Service endpoint.

section.title: Service discovery (ONVIF Core GetServices)
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls ONVIF Core GetServices on the Device Service endpoint.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns GetServiceResponse including the AI Service entry with MCP endpoint URL (example: https://192.0.2.10/mcp).

section.title: Session initialization
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls server/discover to obtain the device identity, supported protocol versions, and capability flags.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns its identity, the list of supported protocol versions, and its capability flags.

Legacy client rejection (informative): A legacy client connecting with a pre-2026-07-28 protocol version (for example via an initialize request) will receive an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. The ONVIF Device shall not support protocol versions prior to 2026-07-28 and shall always include the supported list so that the client can retry.
Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client opens the Streamable HTTP channel to https://192.0.2.10/mcp as defined by MCP 2026-07-28.

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device confirms the channel. No JSON-RPC response body is returned for channel establishment; the device will send notifications/message frames over this channel as events occur.

section.title: AI capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://onvif/ai.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the AI Service capabilities document.

section.title: Optional non-AI capability discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read with URI capabilities://onvif/<service-name> (example: capabilities://onvif/media).
Response (Device to Client — not supported): If the requested service capability is not exposed, the ONVIF Device returns a resource-not-found error.

section.title: Schema resource inventory
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/list to enumerate all resources, including LinkML schema resources.

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns available resources. Resources with mimeType: application/linkml+yaml are the schema files to be retrieved in (example URIs: linkml://onvif/ai/events/v1).

section.title: Schema retrieval
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends resources/read for each application/linkml+yaml resource URI obtained from (example: linkml://onvif/ai/events/v1).

Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the LinkML schema as a YAML string in the text field. The ONVIF Client registers this schema in its validator. If multiple schema resources were listed in , this request is repeated for each URI.

section.title: Tool discovery
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client sends tools/list to obtain the catalogue of available Skills.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns one Tool entry per supported Skill, each with a compiled inputSchema derived from the LinkML model. The example shows get_status only.

section.title: Skill invocation — get_status
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls get_status with no arguments.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the current state of the AI engine, the list of active analytics types, and the engine firmware version.

section.title: Skill invocation — list_analytics
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls list_analytics with no arguments.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns all analytics types it supports, their enabled state, and the LinkML schema URI that governs the configure_analytics call for each type.

section.title: Skill invocation — configure_analytics
section.para: Request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls configure_analytics specifying the analytics type and a config object whose structure matches the LinkML class identified by configSchema (obtained from list_analytics).
Response (Device to Client — validation error): If the config object violates a schema constraint, the ONVIF Device returns a structured error identifying the failing field.

section.title: Metadata stream — channel opening and event frame
section.para: Channel opening (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client opens the Streamable HTTP channel to https://192.0.2.10/mcp as defined by MCP 2026-07-28. No JSON-RPC request/response exchange occurs for channel establishment; the ONVIF Device will push notifications/message frames over this channel as events are produced.
Event frame (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device sends a notifications/message frame for each metadata event. The example below shows a FireDetectionEvent carrying a SOSAObservation payload.

section.title: Dynamic schema re-registration
section.para: This example shows the procedure triggered when the ONVIF Client receives a notifications/message frame whose @context URI (linkml://onvif/ai/events/v2) is not yet registered in its schema bundle. The client suspends validation, fetches the schema, and registers it before resuming.

para.emphasis: Incoming frame with unknown context (Device to Client):

section.para: Schema fetch request (Client to Device): The ONVIF Client calls resources/read with the unknown @context URI.
Response (Device to Client): The ONVIF Device returns the new schema. After registration the client validates the suspended event and resumes normal processing.
